item.title: Basic Controls Guide
item.description:
🎮 Basic Controls Guide

In Human: Fall Flat, Bob’s wobbly body has two independently controlled arms. Every keyboard/mouse input is converted into torque output for his wobbly muscles. This guide will help you build muscle memory and master the fundamental movement physics.

📸 Basic Climb: Grab the ledge with both hands, look down, and pull yourself up.

⌨️ Input Command Terminal

Familiarize yourself with the default key bindings to coordinate Bob’s limbs:

  • Move Walk: Use WASD.
  • Rotate Head/View: Move your Mouse. Bob’s hands reach toward the center of your crosshair.
  • Left Grab: Hold Left Mouse Button. Left hand sticks to the target.
  • Right Grab: Hold Right Mouse Button. Right hand sticks to the target.
  • Jump: Press Space. Jumping carries forward momentum when moving.
  • Run: Hold Shift. Bob bends over slightly and accelerates.

📐 Mechanics & Core Movement Systems

1. Grab & Release System

  • The Physics: As long as you hold down the Left/Right Click, Bob’s hands act as high-strength sticky pads. Any surface (walls, boxes, teammates) will be stuck tight.
  • Tip: Release the mouse buttons to let go. When carrying objects, keep the hands flat and pull backwards to slide items smoothly.

2. Standard Wall Climb (Step-by-Step)

This is the most critical hurdle for new players. Master this 4-step sequence:

  1. Approach & Look Up: Move up to the wall, look straight up at the sky, and raise both hands high.
  2. Jump & Grab: Press Space to jump. Ensure both hands stick to the top ledge of the wall. Keep holding the mouse buttons!
  3. Pull Up (Look Down): Slowly move your mouse down to look at the ground. Bob will naturally pull his torso up to the ledge.
  4. Forward Over: While looking down, press and hold W. Bob will swing his legs over and climb on top.
【Climbing Tip for Beginners】
Many beginners fail because they release the mouse buttons too early when trying to step onto the ledge. Remember: Never release your mouse clicks until both feet are firmly on top of the wall! Keep looking down until Bob climbs over.

For advanced physics engines techniques, check out our Core Physics Tricks Guide.

item.title: Community Speedrun & Physics Glitches Guide
item.description:
🚀 Community Speedrun & Physics Glitches Guide

While the developers intended Human: Fall Flat to be a slow-paced puzzle platformer, the game’s wobbly physics engine holds secrets that speedrunners have exploited for years. By exploiting collision math, frame-rate physics ticks, and arm stretch limits, you can fly across maps and climb infinite vertical walls.

This guide details the top four community techniques used to break the game’s boundaries.

📸 Glitched Climb: Defying gravity by exploiting Bob's arm-rotation friction physics.

🧗 1. Vertical Flap / Paddling (左右划水爬墙法)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
  • Purpose: Climb completely smooth, flat vertical walls to infinite heights.
  • Theory: When Bob grabs a wall and rotates his camera, the shoulder joint stretches. By alternating left and right grabs while rotating the camera rapidly, you bypass the vertical limit.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Stand facing the wall. Raise both hands and jump to grab as high as you can.
    2. Release your Right Hand only.
    3. Quickly flick your mouse to the right (about 45–60 degrees). This rotates Bob’s hips and shoulder, raising his free right arm higher up the wall.
    4. Grab the wall with your Right Hand at this new height.
    5. Release your Left Hand. Flick your mouse to the left.
    6. Grab the wall with your Left Hand at the new height.
    7. Repeat this rhythm: Release Right -> Turn Right -> Grab Right -> Release Left -> Turn Left -> Grab Left. It will look like Bob is “paddling” or “flapping” up the wall.

🪂 2. Single-Hand Super Swing (单手极限摆荡)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐☆☆
  • Purpose: Swing across massive gaps using a single anchor point, gaining double the normal momentum.
  • Theory: Grabbing with both hands distributes weight evenly but limits swing range. Grabbing with only one hand allows Bob to act as an offset pendulum, creating torque.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Jump toward the swing rope, pipe, or ring, and grab it with only one hand (e.g., Left Hand).
    2. Hold down the forward movement key (W) as you swing forward.
    3. When you reach the peak of the forward swing, do not release. Instead, turn your camera 90 degrees away from the swing direction and press A or D to slide Bob’s body around the rope.
    4. Swing back, and then swing forward again. On the second forward swing, press the keys to twist Bob’s body.
    5. The twisting motion adds rotational velocity. Release the grab at the peak of the second swing to propel yourself twice as far as a normal two-handed swing.

🏹 3. Slingshot Glide / Zipline Inertia (吊索势能惯性弹射)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
  • Purpose: Launch yourself across the map when releasing from ziplines, cables, or swinging chains.
  • Theory: If you release a grab while Bob’s body is stretched to its limit, the physics engine releases the elastic tension instantly. This converts hook tension into pure forward velocity.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Grab a zipline handle or rope.
    2. Slide down to gain speed. As you near the end of the line, hold back (S) to pull your body behind the hook, stretching Bob’s arms.
    3. Suddenly release S and press W. Bob’s body will snap forward like a rubber band.
    4. Release the mouse clicks at the exact microsecond Bob’s body passes directly under the hook.
    5. If timed correctly, the velocity will double, gliding you hundreds of meters in the air.

🖥️ 4. FPS Checkpoint Skip (帧率调节逃课)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐☆☆
  • Purpose: Force Bob to glitch through solid metal gates or skip checkpoint triggers.
  • Theory: Human: Fall Flat calculates collision detection based on frame rate. At extremely high or low frame rates, the physics engine’s tick rate changes, allowing Bob’s wobbly limbs to clip through solid meshes when squeezed.
  • Step-by-Step Execution:
    1. Go to a door or gate with a small gap (like the iron gates in Castle or Dark).
    2. Squeeze Bob’s body sideways into the corner where the gate hinges meet the wall.
    3. Grab the wall inside the gap with both hands and pull hard.
    4. FPS Manipulation: Speedrunners use keybinds or settings to temporarily cap their FPS to 15 (creates physics lag) or unlock it to 300+ (creates high-frequency collision updates).
    5. Wiggle your camera left and right rapidly. The collision solver will fail to calculate Bob’s boundaries in time, popping you straight through to the other side of the gate.

📊 Speedrun Glitch Matrix

Glitch Technique Difficulty Best Maps to Use Approximate Time Saved
Vertical Paddling ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ Mountain, Aztec, Castle 3 - 5 Minutes per map
Single-Hand Swing ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ Mansion, Steam, Water 1 - 2 Minutes per map
Slingshot Glide ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Dark, Thermal, Port 2 - 3 Minutes per map
FPS Checkpoint Skip ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ Castle, Dark, Power 4 - 6 Minutes per map
⚠️ Warning: Glitch climbing and FPS manipulation take hours of practice to master. Start by practicing "Vertical Paddling" on the flat walls in the starting courtyard of Level 1: Mansion.

Want to apply these glitches? Read our Mansion Walkthrough or choose a level from the Level Guides Index to find skips!

item.title: Core Physics Tricks Guide
item.description:
💪 Core Physics Tricks Guide

Once you master basic grabs, you can unlock Bob’s inertia engine. By combining coordinate rotations and friction limits, you can perform advanced movements that bypass standard puzzles entirely.

📸 Swing Jump: Converting gravitational potential energy into forward speed.

🎛️ Training Modules: Advanced Physics Guides

1. The Swing Jump (Pendulum Action)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐☆☆☆
  • Application: Crossing super-wide chasms using ropes, poles, or hanging lanterns.
  • Action Sequence:
    1. Jump and grab the rope/lantern at the highest possible point.
    2. Hold W and S in cycles. Push forward at the peak of the backward swing, and pull back at the peak of the forward swing to build momentum.
    3. Once the swing reaches maximum speed, wait until you reach the highest point of the forward arc (when speed drops to zero for an instant).
    4. Release both grabs instantly, and press Space to launch yourself forward.

2. Single-Hand Wall Climb (Horizontal Wiggle)

  • Difficulty: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
  • Application: Climbing flat vertical walls without any ledges.
  • Action Sequence:
    1. Face the wall, raise one hand (e.g. left hand) and grab it. Leave the other hand free.
    2. Swing your camera to the right, raising the free right hand above the left hand. Grab the wall with your right hand.
    3. Release the left hand click. Swing your camera to the left, raising the left hand above the right hand, and grab.
    4. Repeat this coordinate rotation back and forth to walk your hands up the wall.

🏆 Physics Training Matrix

Trick Name Difficulty Core Mechanism Training Map Recommendation
Swing Jump ⭐⭐☆☆☆ Gravity & Pendulum Swing Mountain, Castle
Glitch Throwing ⭐⭐⭐☆☆ Inertia & Torque Release Carry, Factory
Single-Hand Climb ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ Coordinate Wiggling & Friction Mansion, Mountain
Super Jump ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Frame-Rate Collision Glitch Any flat ground
💡 Tip for Glitch Climb: Always make sure your camera is rotated at least 45 degrees sideways when raising the free hand. This forces Bob's shoulder joints to stretch higher than normal, allowing you to reach further up the wall.

Ready to test your training? Head over to our Level Guides Index to check all 30 official maps!
